title: rate_limiting plugin config
description: The `config` object of an enabled `rate_limiting` plugin, generated from ferrum-edge/ferrum-edge openapi.yaml at v0.9.21 (f9915358c8032214f4034a17c28cdf72d14006c3), component RateLimitingConfig and every component it references. Do not edit: run ci/plugin_config_schemas.py. This is Edge's own configuration schema, governed by Edge's support policy (docs/versioning.md); the plugin catalog records when Edge requires it.

RateLimitingConfig.description: Plugin: rate_limiting — Per-IP, per-consumer, per-SPIFFE-identity, or per-policy aggregate (`limit_by: service`) request rate limiting. Quota 429 responses carry a Retry-After header. On stream proxies, consumer mode uses the identified stream Consumer when available and otherwise falls back to client IP; `spiffe_identity` keys on the SPIFFE ID extracted by the `spiffe_identity` / `mtls_auth` mesh chain and falls back to client IP when no SPIFFE identity is present. Supports centralized Redis-backed mode for coordinating rate limits across multiple gateway instances. `limits` must contain exactly one `scope: default` rule for generic keys and fallback IPs, plus optional `scope: consumers` rules that apply the same rate rule to one or many consumer identities, each with an independent counter. Counter storage supports only local memory and Redis; database-backed counters are intentionally unsupported. Residual admission rules this schema cannot express, enforced by the plugin constructor alone: one consumer identity may not appear in two different `scope: consumers` rules (JSON Schema can only reject a duplicate inside one rule), and `redis_url` details noted on that field.

limit_by.description:
Rate limit key. Parsed case-insensitively; `null` is the same as omitting the field:
- `ip` (default) — client IP.
- `consumer` — identified consumer (HTTP) or stream consumer (TCP/UDP); falls back to client IP when no consumer is present.
- `spiffe_identity` — SPIFFE ID extracted from peer certificate (mesh authn). `spiffe` is accepted as an alias.
- `service` — one aggregate budget per policy shared by every caller (a total route/service rate), charged after authentication (authorize phase) on HTTP and once per connection/session on TCP/UDP. With `sync_mode: redis` the budget is shared by every gateway serving the policy. Compose it beside a per-caller instance to enforce both a per-caller and a total limit.

ipv6_prefix.description: IPv6 prefix length used to group source addresses for IP rate-limit keys. IPv4 addresses remain host-specific.

expose_headers.description: Inject x-ratelimit-* headers on requests and responses. Every admitted (counted) request's client-visible response carries the headers, including successful WebSocket handshake responses and gateway-generated responses such as cache hits, response mocks, serverless short-circuits, and rejections from plugins that run after rate limiting. The header names are one public set, so when several rate_limiting instances run on a route exactly one verdict is published: the limiter that refused the request, or — when all of them admitted — the tightest remaining budget. A refusing limiter with expose_headers=false, and any fail-closed 503, publish no rate-limit headers at all.

max_state_entries.description: Hard cap on distinct keys this policy keeps in local (and Redis-fallback) state. At the cap, keys already tracked keep their budgets and a previously unseen key is refused with 429 until idle keys are pruned. Read per admission and not part of the local-state compatibility fingerprint, so changing it never resets live budgets.

limits.description: Rate-limit rules. Must include exactly one `scope: default` rule. `scope: consumers` rules are only valid when `limit_by` is `consumer`.

mcp_tool_calls.description: Count MCP JSON-RPC tools/call requests instead of HTTP requests (null or omitted counts requests). Only tools/call is charged: each tools/call member of a JSON-RPC batch is one charge, including notification-form tools/call members (a tools/call without an id is still charged); notifications/* methods, initialize, tools/list, and every other method pass uncounted. The charge runs in before_proxy over the buffered body, with the media types mcp_gateway admits (application/json, application/json-rpc, +json, or no Content-Type); a body with duplicate member names, or a batch past 32 members / 1 MiB / 256 KiB per member, is refused with JSON-RPC -32600. So is an in-scope request whose Content-Type declares a charset other than UTF-8, and a body strict UTF-8 JSON cannot read (UTF-16/32, a byte-order mark, NaN, comments, invalid UTF-8) that could still carry a tools/call for a lenient upstream parser. These recognizer bounds are fixed at 32 members / 1 MiB / 256 KiB per member; setting mcp_gateway validation.max_batch_* above these values makes the limiter refuse the larger request with -32600. An in-scope request with non-identity Content-Encoding is refused with JSON-RPC -32017 unless an earlier decompression hook has removed the encoding. An exhausted budget is answered on HTTP 200 with a JSON-RPC error (code -32015, one per request-form batch member) plus x-ratelimit-* headers when expose_headers is set; a fail-closed Redis outage answers -32016. The mode is HTTP-only.

endpoint_path.description: Inspect and buffer only requests to exactly this path (normally mcp_gateway endpoint.path). No query, fragment, or control character.

tools.description: Count only calls naming one of these public tool names. The per-name bound is enforced by the constructor in UTF-8 bytes (maxLength counts characters).

per_tool.description: Keep one budget per listed tool instead of one shared by every counted call. Requires tools.

sync_mode.description: Rate limit state storage: 'local' (in-memory per instance) or 'redis' (centralized across instances), parsed case-insensitively. `redis` additionally requires `redis_url`. Database-backed counters are unsupported. Any RESP-compatible server works (Redis, Valkey, DragonflyDB, KeyDB, Garnet).

redis_url.description: Redis connection URL (e.g., redis://host:6379/0), required with sync_mode=redis. The database selector is a canonical decimal integer from 0 through 2147483647, without signs, zero-padding, or extra slashes. An absent path or bare slash selects database 0. Ferrum uses the portable signed-32-bit bound; redis-rs represents indexes as i64. The server separately checks its configured databases on SELECT. TCP port range is constructor-validated. URL fragments are forbidden; TLS skip-verify is only FERRUM_TLS_NO_VERIFY.

redis_tls.description: Enable TLS for the Redis connection (upgrades redis:// to rediss://; the URL scheme is matched case-insensitively and stored lowercase). CA verification uses gateway-level FERRUM_TLS_CA_BUNDLE_PATH; skip-verify uses FERRUM_TLS_NO_VERIFY.

redis_key_prefix.description: Key prefix for all Redis keys. Defaults to `{FERRUM_NAMESPACE}:{plugin_name}:{plugin-config-id}` so two independent policies of this plugin type in one namespace do not share counters. Setting this explicitly is the documented opt-in for a deliberately shared budget: every instance configured with the same prefix increments and rejects against the same counters.

redis_pool_size.description: Number of multiplexed Redis connections. Must be between 1 and 128.

redis_failure_policy.description: Behavior when the centralized Redis store cannot be consulted: an outage, an egress/DNS screen failure, or an endpoint rejected as an unsupported topology (Redis Cluster is not supported). fail_closed explicitly refuses the request with 503 and no rate-limit headers; local_fallback (the default) uses per-process budgets, which enforce the configured limit once per gateway process. Only meaningful with sync_mode=redis, but validated in either mode.

redis_connect_timeout_seconds.description: Effective Redis connection-attempt timeout in seconds. Applied to the redis-rs inner connection config for cached, dedicated, and health-check paths (TCP connect, TLS handshake when enabled, Redis protocol handshake). It is also the deadline for the proactive `INFO CLUSTER` topology screen (and the no-eviction memory screen) issued on every new connection, on the pooled and dedicated paths as well as the recovery probe — the redis-rs 500ms command cap does not preempt it. That per-command cap is installed on the connection once it is screened, so ordinary command execution stays bounded. Gateway DNS screening/resolution of the Redis hostname runs before this timeout starts.

redis_health_check_interval_seconds.description: Interval in seconds for health check pings when Redis is marked unavailable. Must be greater than zero.

RateLimitingRuleConfig.description: One rate_limiting rule. Every rule must set either one or more preset fields (`requests_per_second`/`requests_per_minute`/`requests_per_hour`) or the custom-window pair (`window_seconds` + `max_requests`), but not both styles in the same rule. Exactly one rule in the plugin config must use `scope: default`. `scope: consumers` is only valid with `limit_by: consumer`; each listed identity gets its own independent counter using this rule's windows.

scope.description: `default` applies to all keys without a more specific consumer rule and to IP fallback. `consumers` selects the identities listed in `consumers`; each identity has its own counter. Parsed case-insensitively.

consumers.description: Effective consumer identities for `scope: consumers` rules. Each listed identity gets an independent counter using this rule's windows. Matched against the mapped Consumer username only; an unmapped external identity never matches, even one that spells a listed username, and is counted under its own realm-scoped key. A repeated identity is rejected here and across rules; JSON Schema can only express the within-rule half, so the cross-rule duplicate is refused by the plugin constructor alone.

requests_per_second.description: Max requests per second. Capped at 1000000 (see `max_requests`).

requests_per_minute.description: Max requests per minute. Capped at 1000000 (see `max_requests`).

requests_per_hour.description: Max requests per hour. Capped at 1000000 (see `max_requests`).

window_seconds.description: Custom rate-limit window length in seconds. Must be paired with `max_requests`. Capped at 2678400 (31 days) so the window stays representable as a monotonic duration and as a signed Redis TTL.

max_requests.description: Maximum requests permitted within `window_seconds`. Capped at 1000000 as an operational budget ceiling. Local sliding-window memory is bounded independently by a fixed aggregate-bucket ring per key, not by one timestamp per admitted request.
